## IWFM files: call iwfm-io, do not reimplement it

This project reads or writes IWFM (Integrated Water Flow Model) files.
The `iwfm-io` package already does that: readers **and** writers for every
dataset in every IWFM input file, output readers (HDF + text), budget
aggregation, 66 plots, GIS/VTK export, and PEST++ calibration support.

**Before writing any function that reads, writes, parses, converts or
aggregates IWFM data, search the API index:**

```bash
iwfm-io api <keyword>          # e.g. iwfm-io api "water year"
iwfm-io api                    # whole index, grouped by intent
```

In Python: `import iwfm_io; iwfm_io.find("water year")`.

If the search returns a match, call it. Write your own only when the
search comes up empty, and say so in a comment so the next reader knows
it was checked.

### Never hand-roll these

Each one has a convention that hand-written code gets wrong:

| Don't write | Call instead |
| --- | --- |
| IWFM date parsing/formatting (`MM/DD/YYYY_24:00`) | `parse_iwfm_date`, `format_iwfm_date` |
| "which day / water year does this stamp belong to" | `iwfm_day`, `water_year` |
| Comment/blank-line skipping while parsing | `IWFMFileReader` |
| Opening a model, finding its files | `open_model(model_dir)`, then `.describe()` |
| Heads, budgets, hydrographs | `.heads_df()`, `.budget_df()`, `read_budget_hdf`, `read_budget_text` |
| Budget rollups to water year / month | `aggregate_budget` |
| Recurring-year (year 2500) series | `expand_recurring` |
| Land-use area tables | `read_land_use_area`, `read_all_land_use_areas` |
| Editing an input file as text | `read_*` -> edit the DataFrame -> `write_*` |
| Copying a model to modify it | `create_scenario` |
| Running the IWFM executables | `run_model` |
| Comparing two runs | `compare_models` |
| Observed vs simulated, SMP files, PEST++ | `iwfm_io.pest` |
| Any plot or map of the above | `iwfm_io.plots` |

### The conventions behind that table

- A stamp like `10/01/1990_24:00` is the **end of Oct 1**: it parses to
  the timestamp `1990-10-02 00:00`, but the value belongs to Oct 1. Take
  the owning day from `iwfm_day`, never from the timestamp's own
  calendar day — that off-by-one silently shifts water-year totals.
- Comment characters are `C`, `c`, `*` in column 1 — and **a leading `/`
  is a data line with a blank value**, not a comment.
- Several IWFM sections are read as "data lines until a comment line",
  so terminating comments are load-bearing: IWFM *counts* the lines of
  some blocks to decide which optional entries exist. The writers emit
  them; hand-patched text does not, and the executables then misread the
  deck.
- Budget `1YEAR`/`1MON` windows are anchored to the simulation start,
  not the calendar. `aggregate_budget` reproduces the DLL exactly,
  including per-component rules (storage terms are not summed).
- Readers are strict: a malformed file raises `IWFMParseError` naming
  the file, section and line. Report that line rather than working
  around it; `open_model(path, strict=False)` keeps what parsed.
- Writers refuse cells IWFM would misread (NaN, `/` inside a name,
  missing layers). Fix the DataFrame — the refusal is the writer
  catching a deck that would not run.

`open_model(path)` then `describe()` is the right first move on any model:
it reports the grid, the simulation period, and which budgets and
hydrographs exist, so nothing downstream has to be guessed.
